The language has 19 operators. A model calls them by name with positional arguments; there are no infix operators yet, so `a + b` is written `add(a, b)`. Every operand is `f32` except the ids of `embedding` and the labels of `cross_entropy`, each its second operand, which are `i32`. The Tensor IR op of `dropout` also reads the RNG token of its call site, an internal `i32[2]` input that no source value supplies, and `sigreg` lowers to `MatMul`, `SigregColumns` and `ReduceMean` over the projection of its call site, an internal `f32[K, M]` input drawn at every step. After its operands an operator may take named compile-time arguments, each required and given once as a literal: `attention` takes `heads` (an integer literal of at least 1); `dropout` takes `p` (a float literal in [0, 1)); `sigreg` takes `slices` (an integer literal of at least 1).

Generated by `modelspec-docs` from the operator registry in [`crates/modelspec-core/src/ops.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-core/src/ops.rs): the type checker, the IR builder and the verifier all type an operation through the one function `ops::infer`, and every example below is its answer.

The type checker reports a refused call as a diagnostic: `E-TYPE-012` for a `matmul` contracting dimension, `E-TYPE-003` for operands of different shapes, `E-TYPE-004` for a rank, `E-TYPE-001` for an argument count, `E-TYPE-018` for an operand of the wrong element type; for a named argument, `E-TYPE-001` when it is missing, `E-TYPE-002` when the operator takes no argument of its name or it is given twice, `E-TYPE-019` for a value that is not a literal of its kind; `E-TYPE-020` for `attention` heads that do not divide the width, `E-TYPE-021` for a key mask, labels or weights that read a parameter, `E-TYPE-022` for a `dropout` `p` outside [0, 1), and `E-TYPE-019` for `sigreg` `slices` of 0; and, beyond the call itself, `E-TYPE-026` for a parameter the loss reads only through `stop_gradient` ([Diagnostics](diagnostics.md)).

## `matmul`

Tensor IR op `MatMul`, 2 operand(s).

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [4, 1]>)` | `Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>` |
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>, Tensor<f32, [3, 1]>)` | refused: `matmul contracting dimension mismatch`: `lhs Tensor<f32, [8, 4]>`, `rhs Tensor<f32, [3, 1]>`, `expected rhs dimension[0] = 4; got 3` |
| `matmul(Tensor<f32, [8]>, Tensor<f32, [8, 1]>)` | refused: `MatMul needs a rank-2 operand; got Tensor<f32, [8]>` |

## Gradients

The reverse-mode rule of each op, for `Y = op(A, B, C)` and `G = dL/dY` (`attention` has a fourth operand `D`, its key mask, which takes no gradient; the labels `B` and weights `C` of `cross_entropy` take none either, nor does the RNG token `B` of `dropout`, and `stop_gradient` passes none back at all), from the doc comment of `ops::gradient`. `modelspec-runtime`'s gradient tests check every rule against central finite differences.

| op | `dA` | `dB` | `dC` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Add` | `G` | `G` | |
| `Sub` | `G` | `-G` | |
| `Mul` | `G * B` | `G * A` | |
| `MatMul` | `G @ transpose(B)` | `transpose(A) @ G` | |
| `Relu` | `where(A > 0, G, 0)` (`ReluGrad`; 0 at `A = 0`) | | |
| `Transpose` | `transpose(G)` | | |
| `ReduceSum` | `broadcast_scalar(G, shape(A))` | | |
| `ReduceMean` | `broadcast_scalar(G * (1 / numel(A)), shape(A))` | | |
| `Mse` | `(A - B) * (G * (2 / numel(A)))` | `-dA` | |
| `Embedding` | `embedding_grad(B, G, rows(A))` (`EmbeddingGrad`: row `G[n]` added to row `B[n]`) | none: `B` is `i32` ids | |
| `AddRows` | `G` | `sum_rows(G)` (`SumRows`: the rows of `G` summed in ascending order) | |
| `Gelu` | `gelu_grad(A, G)` (`GeluGrad`: `gelu'(A) * G`) | | |
| `LayerNorm` | `layer_norm_grad_x(A, B, G)` (`LayerNormGradX`: `rstd * (G B - mean(G B) - xhat * mean(G B xhat))` per row) | `layer_norm_grad_gamma(A, G)` (`LayerNormGradGamma`: the rows of `G * xhat` summed in ascending order) | `sum_rows(G)` |
| `Softmax` | `softmax_grad(Y, G)` (`SoftmaxGrad`: `Y * (G - rowsum(G * Y))`) | | |
| `Attention` | `attention_grad_q(A, B, C, D, G)` (`AttentionGradQ`: `scale * dS K` per sequence and head) | `attention_grad_k(A, B, C, D, G)` (`AttentionGradK`: `scale * dS^T Q`, 0 at a masked key) | `attention_grad_v(A, B, C, D, G)` (`AttentionGradV`: `P^T G`, 0 at a masked key) |
| `CrossEntropy` | `cross_entropy_grad(A, B, C, G)` (`CrossEntropyGrad`: `G * C[n] / sum(C) * (P[n, v] - [v = B[n]])`) | none: `B` is `i32` labels | none: `C` is constant weights |
| `Dropout` | `dropout_grad(B, G)` (`DropoutGrad`: `G * (1 / (1 - p))` where the mask of token `B` keeps the element, 0 elsewhere) | none: `B` is the `i32` RNG token | |
| `StopGradient` | none: no gradient flows back through it; the pass `passes::stop_gradient` replaces it by `A` after autodiff | | |
| `SigregColumns` | `sigreg_columns_grad(A, G)` (`SigregColumnsGrad`: `2 G[m] sum_j c_j t_j (S_j cos(t_j A) - (C_j - phi_j) sin(t_j A))` in column `m`) | | |
